products.title: Booking Demo v1
products.description: 58 fictional event-booking rows across four related tables, in JSON, CSV and SQLite, with three checked SQL journeys covering capacity, refunds and empty states.

preview.title: Booking Demo v1
preview.description: 58 fictional event-booking rows in JSON, CSV and SQLite, with three checked SQL user journeys.

schema_summary.customers: customer_id primary key; display_name, example.com email, created_at
schema_summary.events: event_id primary key; title, starts_at, venue, capacity, price_cents, USD currency
schema_summary.bookings: booking_id primary key; customer_id and event_id foreign keys; seats, status, unit_price_cents, total_cents, created_at, nullable cancelled_at
schema_summary.payments: payment_id primary key; booking_id foreign key; kind, status, amount_cents, nullable parent_payment_id self-reference, occurred_at

semantics: All identities and transactions are fictional; timestamps are UTC ISO 8601.
Money is integer USD cents, unrelated to the native ETH used to buy the package.
Only confirmed seats consume capacity; pending reservations do not hold seats.
Only succeeded charges and refunds affect net received; failed attempts count as zero.
Refund amounts are positive and reference a successful charge on the same booking.
Booking and payment totals must be aggregated separately to avoid inflated seat counts.
Each full-product journey runs on its own baseline copy and includes exact SQL results.

sample_journey.title: A cancelled booking has a charge and matching refund
sample_journey.sql: SELECT b.booking_id, b.status, SUM(CASE WHEN p.status != 'succeeded' THEN 0 WHEN p.kind = 'charge' THEN p.amount_cents ELSE -p.amount_cents END) AS net_cents FROM bookings b JOIN payments p ON p.booking_id = b.booking_id WHERE b.booking_id = 'b1004' GROUP BY b.booking_id, b.status;
